value.body: State forest departments recruit Assistant Conservators of Forests (ACF) and Range Forest Officers (RFO) to protect forests and wildlife, run plantations and nurseries, handle forest offences and work with forest-dwelling communities. ACFs manage a sub-division; RFOs manage a forest range on the ground.

items.label: Recruited by
items.value: State PSC (in some states a separate forest recruitment board)

items.label: Typical eligibility
items.value: A graduate degree in a listed science subject, often including Forestry, Agriculture, Botany, Zoology or Engineering

items.label: Also required
items.value: Physical standards and a walking test

items.label: Promotion quota into Indian Forest Service
items.value: Up to ~33% of a state's IFS cadre
items.note: Filled by promoting State Forest Service officers; the rest is direct recruitment through UPSC
items.source: IFS (Recruitment) Rules, 1966, as summarised by UPSC

items.label: Posts in recent state notices
items.note: Examples: HPPSC 8 ACF posts (2025); GPSC 26 ACF/RFO posts (2026); MPPSC 36 ACF and Forest Ranger posts (2025–26); UKPSC 46 posts including Logging Officer (2025)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Apply when your state notifies ACF or RFO posts. Selection is usually a written exam (general studies plus optional or science papers), a physical/walking test, and an interview for some posts. Selected officers then go through institutional training.

value.title: At a glance
items: Some states give preference to forestry graduates; the rules differ by state.
State Forest Service officers can later be promoted into the Indian Forest Service.
Postings are often in remote forest areas.
